messages:
mishal: Quick heads-up — I ran a trace-based sim on last week's EU evening burst. Warmup/waste is showing up as the dominant hit to effective throughput, not pure capacity limits. We should decide mitigation before next weekend.

 dario: What do you mean by warmup/waste here? like model loading time? :thinking_face: 

 mishal: Lots folded in: model binary pull + GPU kernel warmup + KV-cache cold refill. In our sim the first ~3 minutes of each scaled-up GPU deliver ~30–40% of steady tokens/sec, then ramp. With short 6–12m bursts that kills efficiency.

 dario: Can you paste the sim numbers so we can eyeball cost impact?

 mishal: Sure — pasted the micro calc I used: 
```
burst_peak_rps = 420 req/s (EU evening)
avg_seq_len = 900 tokens
steady_tokens_per_gpu = 4800 tok/s
assume 1 GPU handles ~ (4800 / (avg_seq_len)) ~ 5.3 concurrent streams at steady state
-> required_gpus_steady = ceil((burst_peak_rps * avg_seq_len) / steady_tokens_per_gpu) ~ 79 GPUs
warmup_effective_pct = 0.35 for first 180s
effective_tokens_during_warmup = steady_tokens_per_gpu * warmup_effective_pct
wasted_capacity_pct_on_warmup = 1 - warmup_effective_pct = 0.65
if we scale 20 GPUs from 0 for an 8m burst, wasted_gpu_minutes ~= 20 * 8 * 0.65 = 104 gpu-minutes (~1.73 gpu-hours)
cost_impact_est = 1.73 * $3.40 (eu g4-style price) = ~$5.9 per short burst
```

andre: Interesting — that matches what I saw in the pool metrics. Cold pulls from model-registry in eu-west-1 are ~300–600ms per shard and KV-cache refill depends on request fanout. Network/registry latency is non-trivial.

 tanya: So either we pay this waste repeatedly or keep a small warm pool. What's the math for pre-warmed vs cold scale?

 mishal: Quick back-of-envelope: prewarm_pool = 8 GPUs kept idle-but-warmed. Idle cost = 8 * 1 * $3.40 = $27.2/day (if kept 24h). If we only see 2 small bursts a day that would be $54 vs cold-warm cost 2 * $5.9 = $11.8 — so prewarm only pays when bursts are frequent or when tail latency/regressions matter.

 dario: Maybe do hybrid: keep a tiny warm pool in high-risk windows (18:00–22:00 EU) and do fast prefetching for model weights right before expected ramp. Also simulate using last 90 days of traces to pick windows.

 ops-bot: autoscale: observed warm-start penalty spike on pool gpu-eu-3 at 2026-03-15T19:07Z — 62% drop in tokens/sec for 150s. See /metrics/pools/gpu-eu-3/warmup.

 andre: We should also look at region-local model-cache replication. If registry read is the bottleneck, replicate model blobs to eu-west-1 and serve from local object store — reduces shard pull from 500ms to ~20–50ms. Ops infra already supports async sync.

 tanya: Another lever: batch window tuning during ramp. If we accept slightly higher latency for the first 30s, we can batch more and reduce GPU count needed. Need to measure impact on 95th pct latency.

 mishal: Proposed next actions:
- run the trace sim across last 90 days and produce per-day wasted_gpu_hours for EU (by 1h buckets)
- add warm-pool cost calc and break-even thresholds for windows
- test model-blob replication on a canary pool (eu-west-1) and measure pull times
- evaluate a simple warm-start policy: keep N prewarmed GPUs for 18:00–22:00 local time and scale otherwise

 dario: +1. I can own the sim sweep and produce a CSV output with columns: date, hour, peak_rps, required_gpus_steady, wasted_gpu_minutes_cold, warmed_pool_savings_est. ETA EOD tomorrow.

 andre: I'll prototype the registry replication and run a 1-day canary during the next EU window.

 tanya: I'll run a short perf test on batching knobs during warmup to see 95p tradeoffs.

 mishal: Great — if sim shows >10 gpu-hrs/week wasted in EU evening we move to warm pool + replication. Thanks all. :rocket:
